verdict_A: NOT FOUND in any of the 7 papers (provisional for Bakirov-Szekely original, which was not obtained). No paper treats finite-population stratified SRSWOR, within-stratum shift/common-scale equivariant intervals, design-variance shares v_h, max-shares kappa_h, two-point-population configurations, a knapsack frontier or the box class (keyword scans for finite population / stratum / hypergeometric / without replacement / design-based returned zero hits in all full texts). Nearest structural analogues only: Poetscher-Preinerstorfer Thm 5.1 / Thm A.5 (valid size-controlling critical value exists iff no extreme-leverage configuration, over Gaussian covariance classes incl. clustered classes), Ibragimov-Mueller 2010 Thm 1 (worst case = k equal variances, rest zero), Kojevnikov-Song Thm 3.1/4.1 (asymptotic impossibility with one large cluster). All are Gaussian/symmetric or asymptotic, not finite-population sampling.
verdict_B: NOT FOUND. No paper compares pooling many strata against the iid threshold in draws per stratum. Related but different: Hagemann Thm 2.1 (exact size 2^-min(q1,q2) for symmetric heterogeneous variables, q>=4 clusters give 6.25%), CRS 2017 Thm 2.1 with sign-change group G={-1,1}^q (finite-sample validity needs 2^q large enough, i.e. the log2 threshold in number of clusters/observations), IM10 Thm 1 (valid at 5% for any q>=2 but under Gaussian cluster estimators). These count clusters under symmetry/Gaussianity assumptions; they are baselines for B, not B.
verdict_C: NOT FOUND. None of the 7 papers mentions prediction-powered inference, difference estimators with labelled subsets, or labelling whole clusters versus a few units per cluster (zero hits for prediction-powered / conformal / survey-design terms; 'survey' appears only for CPS data in Mueller and in references). No ACS or states example of the type in C.
verdict_K: PARTLY ADJACENT, NOT EXACT. Szekely (arXiv math/0610838, read fully) Thm 2.1 and Thm 3.1/Cor 1-2 plus Table 1 give certified critical values and extremal configurations (cube-vertex sphere covering; k equal nonzero scales) for the t-statistic over symmetric and Gaussian-scale-mixture classes, with the usual t critical value valid for a>=sqrt3; the same result is restated as IM10 Thm 1 (Bakirov-Szekely 2005, original not obtained). The class there is defined by symmetry/scale mixture on random errors, not by a bound on max|x-mean|/SD or on the largest share of one value in the sum of squares, and not for fixed finite populations or two-point extremals of that type. Hagemann, CRS, IM16, Mueller, KS and PP contain no such class. Caveat: not among the assigned papers but cited in them and probably closer to K: Eaton (1974, bounded linear combinations), Edelman (1990), Dufour (1991) and Dufour-Hallin (1993, 'Improved Eaton bounds for linear combinations of bounded random variables') and Efron (1969); they were NOT read and should be checked before claiming K is new.
deviations: Bakirov & Szekely 2005/2006 original (Zap. Nauchn. Sem. POMI 328 / J Math Sci 139) not obtained: mathnet.ru returned HTTP 403, Springer is paywalled. Substituted Szekely's arXiv math/0610838 (read in full, 7 pp), IM10 Thm 1, and abstracts; verdicts for this paper are provisional.
Mueller 'A More Robust t-Test': read the arXiv v1 (Jul 2020, 57 pp) and the Nov 2022 author-page version (64 pp); the published REStat version was not obtained.
Canay-Romano-Shaikh: main paper only; Econometrica supplement (with proof of Thm 2.1) not read. IM10: accepted-version PDF read; the extended Harvard/SSRN version not read.
